newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two killed in Russian railway station blast.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Russian railway station blast.

text.p: A powerful explosion ripped through a railway station in the southern Russian town of Armavir on Wednesday, killing two people and wounding up to 20, local police said.
A police duty officer in the nearby city of Krasnodar said by telephone the blast had thrown parts of one of the bodies across the station.
Police and troops sealed off the station and the track and used strong floodlights to search for possible bombers, Itar-Tass news agency said. Rail traffic was halted.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the early evening blast, but Tass said an explosive device may have gone off in a passenger's bag at the ticket office or in the waiting room.
It identified the dead as a woman and a man, and said the latter may have been carrying an explosive device. A child was among the eight to 20 people injured, it said.
Interfax news agency said up to nine people had been hurt, three of them seriously, and that all the station's windows had been smashed.
Armavir is about 320 km (200 miles) from the separatist region of Chechnya, and the railway line goes to the Chechen capital Grozny.

Radical separatist rebels in Chechnya have threatened to stage attacks on Russian cities to commemorate the anniversary of independence leader Dzhokhar Dudayev's death in a Russian rocket attack on April 21 last year.

But Chechen vice-president Vakha Arsanov, who is standing in for President Aslan Maskhadov while he is away on a Moslem pilgrimage, denied any Chechen involvement in the incident and blamed it on Russian special security forces.
Tass quoted Arsanov as denying the "Chechen resistance forces" carried out the blast. Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev told Tass he was ready to help Russian security forces solve the case.

Separatist rebels staged two bloody hostage-taking raids outside Chechnya during their almost 21-month conflict with Russia. A ceasefire was agreed last August but talks are bogged down over the region's demands for complete independence.
There were also several blasts on the Moscow transport network during the Chechnya conflict. Police have failed to solve those cases.
Tass said President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had been informed of the blast.
It quoted the regional security chief, Yevgeny Vorontsov, as saying a passenger train had been waiting just outside the station at the time of the explosion.
